text:
alex: Heads-up — after yesterday's prefetch/scheduler change I'm seeing a latency tail increase on medium-length prompts (256-512). Started a few canary runs and grabbed an nsys capture.

priya: ugh, saw a few anomalies in the test dashboard too. Which change exactly? commit hash?

alex: the change is 8f3b9a2 — switched from coalesced-prefetch to eager-prefetch for short KV hits, plus a scheduling tweak to prefer earlier-ready batches.

mateo: can you paste the nsys timeline?

alex: pasted snippet from nsys + perfetto. note the idle gaps between kernel launches around seq len ~320.

```
# nsys summary (trimmed)
GPU  time_start   time_stop    kernel
0    12.2345      12.2358      attention_kernel
0    12.2361      12.2374      kv_prefetch
0    12.2380      12.2400      attention_kernel
# there are 300us gaps where we used to have continuous stream
```

priya: hmm 300us gaps would kill throughput on short tokens. Did the batching heuristic change too?

alex: yes the scheduler now fires a batch as soon as earliest-ready reaches 4 items (was 8), intent was to reduce tail for small requests, but combined with eager-prefetch we see prefetchs that start then get cancelled when a faster request arrives. That handshake seems to serialize and add stalls.

jane: do we have before/after traces for the same workload?

alex: yes. Before (7e2c4d6) shows continuous kernel chain, after (8f3b9a2) shows kv_prefetch launches that are 100-300us separate and a higher number of small attention kernels.

sam: can you bisect to the commit that introduced the scheduler threshold change? maybe the prefetch switch alone is fine.

alex: started bisect — initial results point to scheduler change as the bigger culprit. Reverted eager-prefetch in a variant and latency didn't recover fully; reverting the smaller batch threshold brought latency back to baseline.

mateo: interesting — so smaller batch threshold increases number of kernel launches; combined with prefetch cancellation causes extra serialization. Any perfetto flame screenshots?

alex: attached perfetto timeline excerpt inline:

```
# perfetto timeline (time in ms)
[12.230] kv_prefetch start
[12.232] kv_prefetch end
[12.233] attention launch
[12.234] attention end
[12.237] kv_prefetch start (cancel)
[12.240] attention launch (small)
```

priya: that cancel line stands out. Is the cancellation implemented with a soft flag that forces the kernel to wait on a host-side handshake?

alex: yes — cancellation path does a host acknowledgement to avoid writing stale KV entries. That host round-trip is ~150-250us in these traces.

jane: maybe switch cancellation to a deferred cleanup (post-write GC) for short-lived prefetches? or coalesce cancellations so we avoid the host handshake on the hot path.

sam: or we can change scheduler to avoid firing batches below 6 unless latency SLO requires it. Might be a safer rollback.

mateo: have we quantified cost in tokens/sec and p95? numbers would help.

alex: quick numbers from experiment cluster (same model, concurrent 60qps, seq=384):
- before: p95=82ms, tokens/s=114k
- after (both changes): p95=122ms, tokens/s=86k
- revert prefetch only: p95=110ms, tokens/s=95k
- revert scheduler only: p95=84ms, tokens/s=112k

priya: thanks. seems scheduler tweak is primary. Can you file a rollback PR for the threshold and open follow-ups for prefetch cancellation rework?

alex: filing now. convo summary in PR and attaching nsys captures + perfetto link.

infra-bot: deploy bot: Canary of revert-pr-412 pushed to canary cluster ci-canary-17 at 2055012730 :rocket:

mateo: nice. once canary stabilizes let's run a head-to-head nsys capture and compare kernel launch deltas.

alex: will do. also adding a small test that simulates rapid arrival order changes to catch the cancellation handshake regression in CI.

jane: thanks team — good catch. :thumbsup:
